en.title: Marches, gatherings and road closures in CDMX on September 15
en.summary: Various demonstrations, parades and patriotic celebrations scheduled for September 15 in Mexico City are expected to cause traffic disruptions across multiple areas.

en.title: Sister of Claudia Tacoronte demands justice for student's murder; "Nothing prepares you for this", she says
en.summary: The sister of a slain student criticized organizers of an academic mobility program for sending students to areas with inadequate security.

en.summary: The US Supreme Court ruled against Trump regarding mail-in voting procedures, which Trump characterized as a significant loss for the country.

en.summary: Various demonstrations are planned to begin at 4 p.m. on September 15, with authorities expecting traffic impacts in affected areas.

en.summary: The city's mobility authority announced special schedules for major transport services during Independence Day, along with changes to bike-sharing and bike parking stations.

en.title: Trump attacks Court for not limiting mail-in voting
en.summary: Trump criticized the U.S. Supreme Court for rejecting his attempt to restrict mail-in voting ahead of November's elections.

en.summary: Trump attacked the Supreme Court after it rejected his request to lift an order blocking his plan to restrict mail-in voting, accusing the court of being intimidated by Democrats.

en.title: Claudia Tacoronte's sister questions why UGR assigned her Morelos as destination
en.summary: The sister of a 21-year-old University of Granada student killed in Morelos during a mobility exchange program has questioned the university's assignment of that destination and expressed frustration from her family regarding the program's organization.

stories.title: Gobernadora de Morelos apunta a "avances significativos" en investigación del asesinato de Claudia Tacoronte

en.title: Morelos governor points to "significant progress" in investigation of Claudia Tacoronte's murder
en.summary: The governor of Morelos state stated that the investigation into the death of Spanish exchange student Claudia Tacoronte in Cuautla has made significant progress and pledged authorities will identify the responsible party.

en.title: Brent crude exceeds 107 dollars

en.title: Brent crude exceeds 107 dollars at opening amid concerns over Saudi supply
en.summary: Oil prices rose more than one percent following attacks on Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure that disabled the kingdom's East-West pipeline.

en.title: Primark Arrives in Mexico Behind Powerful Business Family
en.summary: Fashion retailer Primark, established in Dublin in 1969 and now owned by Associated British Foods, enters the Mexican market. The parent group operates across food, ingredients, sugar, agriculture, and retail sectors.

stories.title: Sin examen ni tesis, la UNAM abre la opción de una titulación conmemorativa

en.title: Without Exam or Thesis, UNAM Opens Commemorative Degree Option
en.summary: UNAM's Aragón campus will continue its Commemorative Degree Program for a second group of graduates who finished their coursework more than ten years ago.

en.title: From América Móvil to Cemex and Infonavit: The 20 Most Important Mexican Companies Competing in the Big Leagues
en.summary: A ranking identifies Mexico's 20 leading companies competing globally, encompassing state-owned enterprises like Pemex and CFE alongside major private corporations in telecommunications, food, retail, banking, and mining.

stories.title: El déficit fiscal de 3.9% del PIB de Hacienda para 2027 se queda corto; FMI y México Evalúa recomiendan 2.5%

en.title: Mexico's 3.9% fiscal deficit target for 2027 falls short; IMF and Mexico Evalúa recommend 2.5%
en.summary: Mexico's Treasury proposes a 3.9% fiscal deficit for 2027, but the IMF and Mexico Evalúa recommend 2.5% instead. Higher deficits increase public debt and interest payments, leaving fewer resources for public services.

stories.title: Estos 3 bancos ofrecen créditos de hasta 500,000 pesos para Pymes que buscan crecer y financiarse

en.title: These 3 banks offer loans up to 500,000 pesos for SMEs seeking to grow and finance themselves
en.summary: Three banks are offering loans of up to 500,000 pesos for small and medium-sized businesses looking to expand. Interested entrepreneurs can apply for these credit products directly at these banking institutions.
